derived_reference_checks.interpretation: The standard-state reaction enthalpy is a thermodynamic lower-bound reference for the chemical reaction duty. The reported microwave energy is about 5.9 times this enthalpy. This ratio is not an efficiency: the reported process value has a source-specific meter boundary, and sensible heating, losses, plasma coupling, gas handling, separation and other loads are not reconciled here.

Only the charged alpha product's kinetic-energy component is directly accessible to an electrostatic charged-particle converter in the basic D-T reaction partition. The neutron component is neutral and must be treated as a separate blanket/thermal path unless a separately qualified neutral-particle conversion mechanism is specified. This arithmetic does not imply the alpha energy is captured by a converter: confinement, plasma heating, exhaust fraction, interception, conversion, conditioning and whole-plant parasitics remain separate.

Using the paper's rounded reported power values, suppressor-grid power is subtracted from gross recovered power. The derived net is 67 W and approximately 48.55% of 138 W, consistent with the paper's rounded 48% report. This is a check of the stated TMX test boundary, not a whole-plant or fusion-born energy efficiency.

This derives charged-product energy share from the source's simplified fuel-mixture model. It is not a direct-conversion efficiency, particle collection fraction, fusion gain or net plant electricity. The model's higher D-He3 temperature/density, side reactions and omitted stability/ignition physics remain separate constraints.
